parsed.explanation: No traveller-facing exposure is documented: no criminalisation, no facility/border/custody restriction, no state targeting; self-ID, conversion-practice ban, equal marriage and a long reform history are climate signals of trans-respecting institutions. Border and custody questions are open, not exposures. The negatives are societal: police-recorded gender-identity hate incidents rose 42% year on year (an undercount by police' own account), and a national survey finds ~1 in 5 trans people threatened with violence and 8% physically assaulted over four years — real tier-3 hostility with a worsening street climate, not mere friction. Recourse exists and operates: police record and publish hate data, law reform proceeds, statutory gains hold. No universal-exposure measure or organised, state-tolerated targeting appears. Documented hostility with functioning (if imperfect) institutions places this in reduced risk, below acceptance-plus-working-protection tiers.
